title: Nintendo Platforming Foundations
blurb: Nintendo's own console-defining run, joined by Rare's technically dazzling Donkey Kong Country trilogy.

games.title: Super Mario World
games.blurb: The SNES pack-in that redefined the platformer with Yoshi, the world map, and secret exits — Europe waited about two years after Japan's 1990 launch title release.

games.title: Super Mario World 2: Yoshi's Island
games.blurb: A hand-drawn, crayon-and-watercolor art style wrapped around one of the most inventive platformers Nintendo ever built, released the same year worldwide.

games.title: Super Mario All-Stars
games.blurb: 16-bit remakes of all four NES Mario games in one cartridge, released simultaneously across Japan, North America, and Europe.

games.title: Donkey Kong Country
games.blurb: Pre-rendered CGI models pushed the SNES's graphics further than almost anything else on the system, reviving the Donkey Kong brand from scratch.

games.title: Donkey Kong Country 2: Diddy's Kong Quest
games.blurb: A darker pirate-themed sequel widely considered the series' peak, released the same year in all three regions.

games.title: Donkey Kong Country 3: Dixie Kong's Double Trouble!
games.blurb: The trilogy's closer, trading some of the pirate theming for a swampy, inventive final adventure.

games.title: Kirby Super Star
games.blurb: Eight compact sub-games in one cartridge, including the two-player Helper system that let a friend control a captured enemy ability.

games.title: Kirby's Dream Land 3
games.blurb: One of the SNES's final first-party releases, arriving so late in the console's life that a European release never materialized.

games.title: Kirby's Dream Course
games.blurb: A golf-meets-pinball hybrid where Kirby himself is the ball, an unusually experimental format for the character.

title: Action-Adventure & Metroidvania
blurb: A Link to the Past and Super Metroid anchor a chapter full of Quintet's atmospheric action-RPGs, one of which never left Japan under its English name until a year after release.

games.title: The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past
games.blurb: The template for nearly every top-down Zelda that followed, including the Dark World mechanic that doubled the game's map.

games.title: Super Metroid
games.blurb: Widely considered the high point of 2D Metroid, released the same year worldwide and still cited as a genre-defining Metroidvania.

games.title: Illusion of Gaia
games.blurb: An atmospheric action-RPG following a boy's journey around a fictionalized real-world map, released in Japan as Gaia Gensouki the year before.

games.title: Terranigma
games.blurb: Released in Japan as Tenchi Sōzō the year before — this one never received a North American release at all, one of the most requested unlocalized SNES RPGs ever.

games.title: Secret of Evermore
games.blurb: An unusual reversal: this action-RPG was developed entirely by Square's North American studio and never released in Japan at all.

games.title: ActRaiser
games.blurb: A genre hybrid alternating side-scrolling action with light city-building sim sections, released in Europe the same year as North America.

games.title: Soul Blazer
games.blurb: Quintet's earlier action-RPG about resurrecting a ruined world town by town, with Europe's release following about a year later.

games.title: Demon's Crest
games.blurb: A moody, atmospheric spin-off starring Ghosts 'n Goblins' gargoyle antihero Firebrand, released in Europe the year after North America.

games.title: The Legend of the Mystical Ninja
games.blurb: A Ganbare Goemon spin-off with Goemon and Ebisumaru renamed Kid Ying and Dr. Yang outside Japan, released the same year in all three regions.

title: Role-Playing Adventures
blurb: Square and Enix's golden age, and the platform where the console RPG genre truly matured — several of these never received any European release at all.

games.title: Chrono Trigger
games.blurb: Widely regarded as one of the best RPGs ever made, pairing time travel with a New Game+ structure years ahead of its time — never released in Europe on SNES.

games.title: Final Fantasy VI
games.blurb: Released in North America as Final Fantasy III, since only two earlier entries had reached the West at the time — no European SNES release ever happened.

games.title: Super Mario RPG: Legend of the Seven Stars
games.blurb: Square and Nintendo's first collaboration, blending Mario's world with turn-based, timed-hit combat — never released in Europe.

games.title: EarthBound
games.blurb: Released in Japan as Mother 2 a year earlier, with a deliberately mundane, present-day setting that stood out against typical fantasy RPGs — never released in Europe.

games.title: Secret of Mana
games.blurb: A real-time action-RPG built around a cooperative three-player mode, released in Europe the year after North America.

games.title: Breath of Fire
games.blurb: Capcom's own entry into the console RPG genre, released in Europe about a year after its North American debut.

games.title: Breath of Fire II
games.blurb: A direct sequel deepening the original's dragon-transformation mechanics — never released in Europe.

games.title: Tales of Phantasia
games.blurb: The first entry in the long-running Tales series — a Japan-only SNES release that never reached the West on this platform at all.

games.title: Live A Live
games.blurb: An anthology RPG spanning wildly different historical eras and playable characters — Japan-only until an official Western localization finally arrived in 2022, 28 years later.

title: Run-and-Gun & Shooters
blurb: Konami's Contra and Gradius sequels anchor a chapter full of genuinely difficult SNES shoot-em-ups, several carrying real regional title changes.

games.title: Contra III: The Alien Wars
games.blurb: Renamed Super Probotector: Alien Rebels in Europe, continuing the same robot-reskin censorship pattern the series carried on NES.

games.title: Super R-Type
games.blurb: A launch-window SNES port of the brutally difficult arcade shoot-em-up, released the same year across all three regions.

games.title: Axelay
games.blurb: A vertical shooter alternating between two visual styles stage to stage, showing off the SNES's Mode 7 scaling technique.

games.title: Gradius III
games.blurb: A home port of the arcade sequel, arriving in the West about two years after its original Japanese release.

games.title: Super Aleste
games.blurb: Renamed Space Megaforce for its North American release, while Europe kept the original Japanese title, Super Aleste — a rare case of only one Western region getting a new name.

games.title: Cybernator
games.blurb: Released in Japan the year before as Assault Suits Valken, with some story content trimmed for the Western Cybernator release.

games.title: Hagane: The Final Conflict
games.blurb: An obscure but well-regarded ninja run-and-gun-platformer hybrid, reaching the West about a year after its Japanese release.

games.title: Sunset Riders
games.blurb: A home conversion of Konami's cowboy-themed arcade run-and-gun, released the same year across regions.

title: Beat-em-ups, Wrestling & Fighting
blurb: Capcom's Final Fight trilogy and Street Fighter II's SNES ports anchor a chapter that also includes one game with three genuinely different regional titles.

games.title: Street Fighter II Turbo
games.blurb: An enhanced SNES-exclusive revision adding faster gameplay and the four boss characters as playable fighters.

games.title: Super Street Fighter II
games.blurb: Adds four new challengers to the roster, released the same year across all three regions.

games.title: Mortal Kombat II
games.blurb: A home port of the arcade sequel, restoring blood via a code — unlike the heavily censored first game's SNES port.

games.title: Final Fight
games.blurb: A home conversion of Capcom's arcade beat-em-up landmark, released in Europe the year after Japan.

games.title: Final Fight 2
games.blurb: A SNES-original sequel skipping arcades entirely, released the same year across regions.

games.title: Final Fight 3
games.blurb: The trilogy's closer, adding selectable special moves and a genuinely large character roster for the genre.

games.title: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles IV: Turtles in Time
games.blurb: Released in Europe as Teenage Mutant Hero Turtles IV, continuing the same UK broadcast-driven rename the franchise carried on other platforms.

games.title: Brawl Brothers
games.blurb: Released in Japan as Rushing Beat Ran and in Europe as Rival Turf! 2, tying it to an earlier Jaleco beat-em-up despite no such numbering in Japan or North America.

games.title: The Ninja Warriors
games.blurb: An unusually scattered regional rollout: Japan's The Ninja Warriors Again, North America's plain The Ninja Warriors, and Europe's Ninja Warriors: The New Generation are all the same game.

title: Puzzle & Party
blurb: A Japan-only Panel de Pon became Tetris Attack for a Western audience that had no idea it wasn't really a Tetris game at all.

games.title: Tetris Attack
games.blurb: Originally Japan's character-driven puzzler Panel de Pon a year earlier — the Western version swapped in Yoshi's Island characters and was branded around Tetris despite having no real connection to it.

games.title: Kirby's Avalanche
games.blurb: A Western-exclusive reskin of Super Puyo Puyo with Kirby's cast replacing the original characters — the only Kirby game never released in Japan.

games.title: Yoshi's Cookie
games.blurb: An unusual case where the North American release actually preceded the Japanese one by about a month.

games.title: Super Bomberman
games.blurb: A four-player-capable entry that helped define the series' multiplayer battle format for the 16-bit era.

games.title: Super Bomberman 2
games.blurb: Adds new power-ups and battle stages, released in the West about a year after Japan.

games.title: Plok
games.blurb: A British-developed platformer-puzzler hybrid about a detachable-limbed hero, released the same year in all three regions.

games.title: Uniracers
games.blurb: A unicycle racer built entirely around chained stunt tricks, released in Europe the following year as Unirally — never released in Japan.

games.title: Wario's Woods
games.blurb: This SNES version is distinct from the earlier NES release — Japan only ever got it via the Satellaview satellite service, never a retail cartridge.

title: Sports & Racing
blurb: F-Zero and Super Mario Kart's Mode 7 tracks anchor a chapter that also holds a surprising number of American-sports titles that made it to Europe anyway.

games.title: F-Zero
games.blurb: A launch-window showcase for the SNES's Mode 7 pseudo-3D scaling, and one of the earliest anti-gravity racers.

games.title: Super Mario Kart
games.blurb: The kart-racing genre's true origin point, released the same year across all three regions.

games.title: Pilotwings
games.blurb: A flight-sim-adjacent launch title built to show off Mode 7's scaling and rotation effects, Europe following about a year after Japan.

games.title: Top Gear
games.blurb: Released in Japan as Top Racer, a Mode 7 racer built by a British studio, published the same year across regions.

games.title: Rock n' Roll Racing
games.blurb: An overhead combat racer from the studio that would later become Blizzard Entertainment, released only in the West.

games.title: NBA Jam
games.blurb: A home conversion of the arcade basketball hit, released across Japan, North America, and Europe the same year — despite being an American sport.

games.title: Ken Griffey Jr. Presents Major League Baseball
games.blurb: A North America-exclusive baseball title, never released in Japan or Europe.

games.title: Madden NFL '94
games.blurb: Released in Japan under different NFL-free branding, this American-football sim still found its way to a genuine European PAL release.

games.title: International Superstar Soccer
games.blurb: A soccer sim released in the West about a year after its Japanese debut, notably getting a real North American release despite the sport's smaller US audience.

title: Simulation & Strategy
blurb: SimCity's SNES port anchors a small chapter that includes three tactical RPGs that stayed in Japan for years, or forever.

games.title: SimCity
games.blurb: A console-exclusive redesign of the PC city-builder with a Mario-themed bonus mode, released the same year across all three regions.

games.title: Harvest Moon
games.blurb: One of the SNES's last major releases anywhere, launching the farming-sim genre with a full day-and-season cycle.

games.title: Ogre Battle: The March of the Black Queen
games.blurb: A tactics-RPG hybrid built around real-time troop movement across a war map, reaching North America two years after Japan — never released in Europe.

games.title: Front Mission
games.blurb: A mecha tactical RPG that launched a long-running series — Japan-only on SNES; the West wouldn't see the franchise until later entries on other platforms.

games.title: Tactics Ogre: Let Us Cling Together
games.blurb: A landmark tactical RPG, Japan-only on SNES — its first Western release came three years later on PlayStation, deliberately timed to avoid clashing with Final Fantasy Tactics.

games.title: Uncharted Waters: New Horizons
games.blurb: An Age-of-Exploration trading and naval-combat sim, released in North America the same year as Japan — never released in Europe.

games.title: Populous
games.blurb: A British-developed god-game classic, ported to SNES the same year across all three regions.

title: Licensed, Movie & TV Tie-ins
blurb: Capcom and Konami's Disney and superhero tie-ins remain some of the best-regarded licensed games of the 16-bit era.

games.title: Disney's Aladdin
games.blurb: Widely considered one of the best licensed platformers ever made, released in North America the year before its European and Japanese debuts.

games.title: The Lion King
games.blurb: A famously difficult platformer built around the film's key scenes, released across Europe and North America the same year.

games.title: Batman Returns
games.blurb: A beat-em-up/platformer hybrid tied to the Tim Burton sequel, released the same year across all three regions.

games.title: Goof Troop
games.blurb: A cooperative puzzle-adventure directed by a young Shinji Mikami, years before he created Resident Evil.

games.title: The Addams Family
games.blurb: A British-developed platformer that reached North America about eight months before its own European release.

games.title: Tiny Toon Adventures: Buster Busts Loose!
games.blurb: A well-regarded platformer starring the Tiny Toons cast, released in Europe about six months after Japan.

games.title: X-Men: Mutant Apocalypse
games.blurb: A licensed beat-em-up/platformer letting players swap between five X-Men, released in Europe the year after North America.

games.title: Jurassic Park
games.blurb: A licensed tie-in blending on-foot action with first-person raptor-hunting sections, released the same year worldwide.

games.title: The Great Circus Mystery Starring Mickey & Minnie
games.blurb: Released in Japan as Magical Adventure 2 — unusually, Europe's release actually preceded North America's by a few months.

title: Cult Classics & Deep Cuts
blurb: Earthworm Jim's absurdist run-and-gun sits alongside a run of Japan-only Square and Human Entertainment titles that stayed unlocalized for decades.

games.title: Earthworm Jim
games.blurb: A surreal run-and-gun starring a sentient earthworm in a robotic supersuit, released the same year across Europe and North America.

games.title: Earthworm Jim 2
games.blurb: A stranger, more level-design-experimental sequel, released in Europe the year after North America.

games.title: Zombies Ate My Neighbors
games.blurb: A cooperative horror-comedy shooter parodying B-movie monster tropes, released the same year across Europe and North America.

games.title: ActRaiser 2
games.blurb: Drops the original's city-building sections entirely in favor of pure action, released in Europe the year after North America.

games.title: Clock Tower
games.blurb: A pioneering point-and-click survival horror game, Japan-only on SNES — its own sequel wouldn't reach the West until PlayStation, years later.

games.title: Bahamut Lagoon
games.blurb: A tactical RPG with dragon-riding mechanics, never officially localized anywhere — only reachable through a long-standing fan translation.

games.title: Star Ocean
games.blurb: The series' Japan-only SNES debut — the West's first taste of it came 12 years later via a PSP remake.

games.title: Umihara Kawase
games.blurb: A cult physics-platformer built entirely around a stretchy fishing line, Japan-only on SNES and largely unknown in the West for decades.

games.title: Robotrek
games.blurb: Released in Japan as Slapstick, this robot-building RPG reached North America the same year — but never Europe.

title: More RPGs & Genre Hybrids
blurb: A second helping of console RPGs and genre-blending curios, several of which stopped at North America and never crossed to Europe.

games.title: The 7th Saga
games.blurb: Released in Japan as Elnard, this six-hero RPG reached North America the same year — but never Europe.

games.title: Lufia & the Fortress of Doom
games.blurb: Released in Japan as Estpolis Denki, launching a series that would return with a well-regarded prequel two years later — never released in Europe.

games.title: Lufia II: Rise of the Sinistrals
games.blurb: A prequel widely considered a major leap over the original, reaching North America the year after its Japanese release.

games.title: E.V.O.: Search for Eden
games.blurb: An evolution-themed action-RPG letting players guide a creature from fish to dinosaur to mammal — never released in Europe.

games.title: Prince of Persia
games.blurb: A home port of the rotoscoped PC platformer classic, released the same year across all three regions.

games.title: Shadowrun
games.blurb: A cyberpunk-fantasy RPG based on the tabletop game — a completely separate, unrelated adaptation from the same-year Sega Genesis game sharing its name and license.

title: Multiplayer, Novelty & Peripheral Games
blurb: Argonaut's Super FX chip games anchor a chapter closing on Star Fox 2, a finished game that didn't officially ship until 2017.

games.title: Mario Paint
games.blurb: A mouse-and-pad peripheral bundle turning the SNES into a drawing and music-composition tool, released the same year worldwide.

games.title: Super Scope 6
games.blurb: A light-gun peripheral bundle of six mini-games, with North America getting the Super Scope itself before Japan or Europe.

games.title: Stunt Race FX
games.blurb: Released in Japan as Wild Trax, this Super FX chip-powered racer used chunky 3D polygon models years before it was common on consoles.

games.title: Star Fox
games.blurb: The Super FX chip's flagship showcase, turning the SNES into a passable 3D rail-shooter machine, released the same year worldwide.

games.title: Star Fox 2
games.blurb: Completed and ready to ship in 1995, then shelved when Nintendo judged its visuals would look dated next to the incoming PlayStation and Saturn — it finally released 22 years later, bundled with the SNES Classic Edition.

games.title: Wolfenstein 3D
games.blurb: A heavily censored SNES port removing Nazi imagery and blood entirely to meet Nintendo's content policy — a striking contrast to the uncensored PC original, which was itself restricted in Germany for decades.

games.title: DOOM
games.blurb: A technically ambitious port of id Software's FPS landmark, built to run on hardware never designed for it — a genuine engineering feat even with the compromises required.

games.title: Mortal Kombat
games.blurb: The infamous SNES port that removed blood entirely under Nintendo's content policy — the Sega Genesis version's now-legendary blood code had no SNES equivalent.
